title: Speaking the Language of Friendship
heading: Speaking the Language of Friendship

sourceRefs.role: active listening and responsive conversation support

coreClaim: Friendship language is conversational behavior that makes the other person feel heard, understood, and worth staying engaged with.
distinctMechanism: Active listening and empathic statements deepen rapport by validating emotional meaning instead of turning the talk back toward the speaker.
requiredAnchors: Listening must stay other-focused rather than performative.
Empathic statements show understanding of emotional content.
specificApplications: Improve one-on-one workplace or school conversations.
Reduce advice-giving that arrives too fast.
Spot canned empathy before it weakens trust.
commonMisreadings: Listening means parroting words back mechanically.
Talking more is the same as connecting more.
hardEdgeRequirement: Hard depth must preserve that conversational empathy fails when it becomes scripted, manipulative, or too obviously strategic.
thresholdQuestion: How do you communicate understanding without sounding artificial or intrusive?
